sq01.name: The Half-Heard Message
steps: [Far, z02] Tamon whispers only the first half of a message for his old neighbour Hanzo ('Tell Hanzo the pear tree still...') and the line cuts out. Mio gets the hanzo_note key item with half a sentence.

[Far, z02] A Dust Wisp that drifted past the pear tree is the only witness. A Glow (lantern held up) makes it hover close; its glow flickers the rest of the sentence in pictures (no combat required, a low-stakes first look at 'the world answers when you are gentle').
[Near, z01/z02] Shift back. Hanzo cannot see ghosts and is gruff. Mio speaks the full message aloud using the Tell verb.
[Both] Hanzo laughs and weeps at once; he leaves a pear at the well. In the Far Shore the pear appears at Tamon's feet. Mio watches the first gentle Crossing.

sq02.name: Kiku's Wind-chime
steps: [Near, z02] Kiku says her wind-chime is 'gone' and that she can see 'a girl with no shoes' near the old tree. She is the only villager who can see the Far Shore, so she gives Mio hints by pointing at empty air.
[Far, z02] The chime hangs on a branch of the tree that is alive only in the Far Shore. A Zashiki Child (shy, lonely) is guarding it, quietly ringing it to feel less alone.
[Far, z02] Choice: take the chime (the child fades into a corner, sad), or tie a loose thread from the chime to make a twin (costs the Far-only 'silk_thread' picked up from the Straw Hound field).
[Near, z02] Return the chime (or the twin). Kiku hears two chimes ring in the Near wind: the Zashiki Child now has one too.

sq03.name: Hollow Roll Call
steps: [Far, z04] Sister Ume shows the register: five names are smudged out. She remembers each person only by their trade ('a lamp-oil seller', 'a boy who rang the bell wrong').
[Far, z04/z05] Five Hollow Villagers wander the shrine floors. Each is a different person. Using Remember on one makes it recite a single clue in battle ('smells of lamp oil').
[Far, z05] Match each villager to a blank in the register by their clue. A correct match makes the Hollow Villager Calm for free; a wrong match only makes the villager restless, not hostile.
[Far, z04] After Send, the name returns to the ledger. The sixth page is blank except for a drawing of a fox sitting at the gate.

sq04.name: The Wrong Note
steps: [Far, z05] Bell Mouse says the shrine bells ring wrong every night. There are three bells on different floors.
[Near and Far, z04/z05] Stand at each bell, Shift, and listen: each bell's pitch is different in the two realms (the Far pitch is the 'true' one the dead remember). Note the order from low to high.
[Far, z05] Kaze's Hum verb plays the true scale; Mio rings the bells in that order (any order retries; the bells chime with the first correct ring).
[Far, z05] Bell Mouse joins Mio's Bond log as a happy neighbour (Bond Lv2).

sq05.name: Oto Waits at the Door
steps: [Near, z08] Hisa says a stray dog sits outside her door every night and is gone by morning; she has never been able to pet him.
[Far, z08] Oto is waiting at the Crossing shop door. He will not cross until she says goodbye.
[Both, z08] Mio places a Lantern Anchor on the shop doorstep: the Far Shore image holds for one scene so Hisa sees Oto. The Anchor costs Lumen but the quest has a Lantern Post right next to it.
[Both] Hisa says goodbye. Oto does not cross; he tells Mio (via bark/ring) that he'll guide others instead.

sq06.name: The Pilgrim Who Never Paid
steps: [Both, z07] Rustle Sprite trades the Remembrance Cord for a Flower Bundle (Marigold Moth Offer or buy in Misty Grove).
[Far, z07-z09] Tie the cord to the Pilgrim (Lumen 2). A glowing thread leads to three short Far-only memory vignettes. His name comes back piece by piece.
[Far, z08] At the Kappa Toll Gate the Pilgrim presses a coin on Mio (toll_token). The Kappa remembers him: he never paid, but the Kappa never collected either.
[Far, z08] Mio chooses: pay the toll (the debt ends, the Kappa forgets him), or leave the debt unpaid (the Kappa keeps the memory but the Pilgrim stays tethered here as a guard).

sq07.name: Feed the Hearth
steps: [Far, z10] Kettle's hearth is cold; nobody has told a story at it for years. A Hearth Brownie lingers by the coals (Bond Lv3 required).
[Near, z10] Three market stallholders each give a memory of a meal (not an item); Mio writes them into Kettle's recipe tin.
[Far, z10] Cook hearth_stew at Kettle's with the three memories as the 'ingredients'. Each memory changes the dish's buff (tracked via the three stalls she visited).
[Far, z11] Serve the stew to the Drowned Clerk (Hollowed, hungry-type). He eats; Mood fills; Send returns his name.

sq08.name: The Lantern Stall
steps: [Far, z11] Ayame has five unlit lanterns; each is inscribed with a family name only readable in the Far Shore.
[Near, z10] Each family lives in Harbor Market (Near). Mio must read the name (Far), Shift, and deliver the lantern (Near).
[Both] Route-plan: Anchor a lantern at the Market square to avoid five round-trip Shifts; each round-trip costs Lumen. A Lantern Post sits at the north gate.
[Near, z10] The final family has no living descendants; Mio lights the lantern herself and leaves it at the Harbor shrine.

sq09.name: The Unfinished Hinge
steps: [Near, z13] Daigo finds a half-forged hinge in the upper mine, hammer marks he recognises as his late master's.
[Far, z14] Only in the Far Shore can the finishing blows be heard: the Oni Foreman (proud) is still working at the master's forge. Fighting him is possible (lv14).
[Far, z14] Proud temper: Rap (+15 Mood) works, Stand (-5) does not. Daigo uses Rap (hammer rhythm) while Mio uses Soothe.
[Near, z14] The Foreman shows Daigo the last three strikes. Daigo finishes the hinge on the Near anvil.

sq10.name: The Tengu's Wager
steps: [Far, z15] The Tengu challenges Mio to a race across three lift shafts; whoever reaches the top first wins.
[Far, z15] Veil Step is required to cross three gaps. The Tengu's gusts push Mio back (timed hazards).
[Far, z15] Mio realises the gusts always come in the same pattern; Kaze can predict them (ghost path shown).
[Far, z15] Mio wins. The Tengu admits that the wager was rigged to make her better.

sq11.name: Marigold Road
steps: [Far, z17] The Pup leads Mio into a marigold field. Petals light only when Mio hums near an ofrenda (altar) of a forgotten household.
[Far, z17] Nine ofrendas are cold. Mio speaks the household's name (Remember) to light each petal; petals are not collected, they are woven as she goes.
[Far, z24] At the Hundred-Step Stair each step takes a petal. The number of petals matters: Name Fragments held (0-30) decide how many floors open (3, 6 or 9).
[Far, z24] The Stair keeper greets Mio. The garland is for the Stair itself.

sq12.name: The Faded Neighbors
steps: [Far, z16] Three Faded Neighbors repeat a loop (sweeping, hanging washing, calling a child). Each loop is a short observable pattern.
[Far, z16] Interrupt the loop at the right moment with the right verb: Remember when the loop breaks, Hum when it repeats, Offer when the neighbour pauses.
[Far, z16/z17] Each success reveals a childhood memory that includes Mio; they faded because Mio stopped visiting after Sachi's illness.
[Far, z16] Send each neighbour; they thank her in their old voices.

sq13.name: A Petal for the Peony
steps: [Far, z18] Ren will stamp the Reader's Card only if Mio brings a petal from the Stone Peony in Still Garden II.
[Far, z19] Three solutions: Parley the Stone Peony (sorrowful, Remember +25), trade it a forgetmenot (Offer), or tear off a petal (fight).
[Far, z19] Parley: the Peony gives the petal willingly. Trade: gives a faded petal. Fight: the Peony turns blank (a 'Blank Peony').
[Far, z18] Ren stamps the card either way, but his greeting changes.

sq14.name: Tea for the Name-Eater
steps: [Far, z19] The Reveler wants a tea party for the three statues in the garden. Each statue is a Hollowed with a different temperament.
[Far, z19] Serve each statue tea matching its temper (Offer with liked items). Each Offer fills Mood; wrong choices only reduce it.
[Far, z20] The Name-Eater joins the party last. It is not malicious: it forgot its own name and devours others'.
[Far, z20] Mio lends her name for one Name Call (she cannot use Name Call for the rest of the dungeon). The Name-Eater releases held Name Fragments.

sq15.name: Lantern Night Procession
steps: [Near, z25] Elder Matsu asks Mio to line up the procession. Each earlier quest completed adds a participant: Hanzo with the pear, Kiku with two chimes, Hisa with Oto, Kettle with stew, Daigo with the hinge.
[Far, z25] The Far side of the procession has the matching spirits: Tamon, the Zashiki Child, Oto, the Brownie, the Pilgrim, the Pup.
[Both] Mio walks the line with the Lantern and lights each carried lantern (one Shift per participant).
[Both] The procession's size determines how many lanterns are visible during the final fight's 'both realms' phase.

sq16.name: The Misfiled Name
steps: [Far, z21] The Owl says one card in the Archive is misfiled; the system keeps it from being found. Three catalog cards cross-reference one another.
[Both, z22] Cards are legible only in the Far Shore, but the shelves exist only in the Near; Mio has to read in one realm and search in the other.
[Far, z22] The misfiled card is Tsubaki's own name, filed under 'Unknown' by Tsubaki herself.
[Far, z23] Mio keeps the card (q_tsubaki_name) and brings it to the final fight.
